subject: Business Models
title: Customer Lifetime Value
description: A short lesson to help you apply Customer Lifetime Value.

hook.text: A Spotify subscriber pays $10/month and stays 4 years on average. That's $480 in lifetime value.

buildup.text: Customer Lifetime Value predicts total revenue from one subscriber over their entire relationship.

discovery.text: CLV determines how much you can spend to acquire a customer. If CLV is $480, spending $50 on ads is rational.

twist.text: Most startups overestimate CLV by underestimating churn. Projected 5-year retention rarely materializes.

climax.text: The CLV-to-CAC ratio is the ultimate subscription health metric. Below 3:1, the business is usually broken.

punchline.text: $480 per subscriber over 4 years. That number funds everything.

quiz.question: What is a healthy CLV-to-CAC ratio?

details.summary: Customer lifetime value estimates the total revenue a subscriber generates over their entire relationship with a business. CLV combines average revenue per user, gross margin, and expected subscriber lifespan. A subscriber paying $50 monthly who stays 24 months has a CLV of $1,200.
details.whyItMatters: CLV determines how much a subscription business can afford to spend acquiring each customer. When CLV significantly exceeds customer acquisition cost, the business has a profitable growth engine. When it does not, growth accelerates losses.
takeaways: CLV calculates total expected revenue from a subscriber over their full lifespan
The CLV to CAC ratio must exceed 3:1 for sustainable subscription growth
Increasing retention is the most effective way to improve CLV

faq.question: How is customer lifetime value calculated for subscription businesses?
faq.answer: Basic CLV equals average monthly revenue per user divided by monthly churn rate. For a $50 ARPU with 4% monthly churn, CLV is $1,250. More sophisticated models discount future revenue and account for expansion revenue, variable margins, and cohort-specific retention curves.

faq.question: Why is the CLV to CAC ratio so important for subscription businesses?
faq.answer: A ratio below 1 means the business loses money on every customer. Between 1 and 3 means profitability is marginal after operating costs. Above 3 indicates a healthy business with room for investment. Above 5 might suggest the company is underinvesting in growth.
